claims.text: Greg Short argues that a fragmented personality -- performing a different version of yourself for each role (student, son, CEO, husband) -- is exhausting and unsustainable, and is one of the primary reasons high-trajectory people burn out before reaching their potential.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: applies to high-trajectory founders and leaders juggling multiple social roles
claims.mechanism: Maintaining multiple distinct personas for different environments consumes cognitive and emotional energy continuously; the cumulative drain makes sustained high performance impossible without eventual collapse.

claims.text: Greg Short asserts that the highest-performing version of a person is a single integrated identity that encompasses all their roles simultaneously -- son, CEO, founder, husband, brother -- rather than switching between context-specific personas.
claims.speaker: Greg Short

examples.text: Greg Short describes his own trajectory: he believed through his 20s that context-switching between distinct personalities (student, son, husband, CEO) was the mark of a sophisticated, adaptable person -- what he called a 'true savage.' It was not until his 30s that he recognized this fragmentation as a liability rather than an asset, and wished he had reached that realization earlier.

practices.text: Stop switching between different versions of yourself for different environments; instead, cultivate one integrated self that is simultaneously son, CEO, founder, husband, and whatever other roles you occupy.
